plans.note: Cap is mutual at greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1M with Excluded Claims defined in 21.3; check adequacy against contract value and confirm data/security and indemnity carve-outs are uncapped, plus 21.2 direct-damages list.

No indemnity article appears in the outline (numbering jumps from 19 to 21), yet Section 9.3 cross-references "Section 20.5" remedies and 21.3 treats indemnification as an Excluded Claim; we likely need to insert a Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity and fix the broken cross-reference.
Second 12.4 imposes a 24-month, all-territory non-compete on Customer, which we reject outright; it also contradicts the protective language in 12.3.
12.3 preserves our supplier freedom, but 7.2's disclose-and-match precondition before engaging another provider and 2.1's take-or-pay operate as de facto exclusivity.
7.2 is a reverse MFN/right of first refusal running against us; wrong direction under the playbook, and it conflicts with 12.3's no-MFN acknowledgement.

First 12.4 bars hiring any Vendor employee for 24 months "regardless of how the employee applies" — needs shortening to 12 months, limiting to personnel involved in the Services, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out consistent with 12.3.

Section 9 contains only breach, insolvency and cause-based rights (no 9.4); no Customer termination for convenience exists and 2.1 expressly denies termination rights — add convenience right on notice with pro-rata refund per 10.2, and confirm Vendor has no reciprocal walk-away.

Auto-renewal with 30-day opt-out plus 60-day reminder and CPI/3% uplift cap in 8.3 is close to playbook; verify notice window and uplift cap are acceptable and interact correctly with 2.1's three-year commitment.
28.1 (Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts) is off-playbook and directly conflicts with 28.2's New York exclusive jurisdiction; resolve to New York law and New York courts.

24.1–24.4 already permit Customer affiliate/successor assignment and bar Vendor exit on our change of control; check 24.3's residual consent requirement does not undercut 24.1 and that 13.3 licence transfer tracks Section 24.

14.1 correctly leaves Customer Data and pre-existing IP with us, but 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of paid-for Deliverables with only a revocable term licence — reverse to Customer ownership (or at minimum the perpetual licence in 13.2) and align with the 1.4 definition.
13.1–13.3 cover Affiliates and contractors and limit revocation, but 14.2's revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence conflicts and must be conformed to the perpetual grant in 13.2.

22.1–22.3 already give annual frequency, 30 days' notice, off-site preference and Vendor-borne cost subject to a 5% shortfall threshold; confirm the threshold and no-system-access limits are retained.

No express liquidated damages clause, but 2.1's take-or-pay shortfall functions as a penalty on us; also confirm interest/late-charge treatment in 7.3 and that service credits (referenced in 1.5) sit in an SLA exhibit that is not in this outline.
90-day Deliverable warranty plus term-long hosted conformity and a repair/refund remedy in 19.4; check the 90-day period is long enough and that 19.5's disclaimer does not erode express warranties.
Coverage lines and limits are present, including USD 5M cyber; verify limits against data sensitivity and that certificates/notice obligations in 18.2 are unconditional.

2.1 imposes a USD 2M/year take-or-pay for three years with no reduction or termination rights and contradicts 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement; delete or add carry-forward, reduction and termination-linked relief.

Section 10 addresses access cut-off, Deliverable delivery and refunds but contains no data-return/export obligation or transition-assistance services; note 16.5 cross-references "Sections 11 and 15" for Customer Data and Section 11 is not in the outline.
